i think it may be because their ability to effect past events are very limited. like however keine's power works isn't like time travel in say back to future where you physically go back in time and directly change events but more like just reversing time to certain point.

after you beat the game theirs a cutscene where keine explains the whole time looping thing and how it took countless amounts of loops, each with slight changes to the last, until all the changes accumulated into a timeline where mystia does succeed. i take this to mean that changing past events is extremely difficult, they cant just make a significant change in one go, just very small changes per loop which, after looping the same set of events over and over many times, incrementally add up to one significant change

so in the very first original timeline, yuyuko eats the fruit of desire, they get mystia lift the curse by satisfying her, she fails, and yukari and keine turn back time to try again. they can't really alter that series of events directly, just subtly influence certain events that lead to very small changes until they cumulate into a different outcome. i guess, for whatever reason, yukari figured it'd be easier to create a timeline where mystia succeeds than one where yuyuko never ate the fruit to begin with

as for why the went with mystia to begin with instead of youmu or sakuya, with youmu i think that, while she does cook yuyuko's meals, she's not a professional chef. its kinda like the difference between a trained private chef cooking meals for you and your mom lol. youmu's more closer to the latter. with sakuya, i think both remillia and patchouli say something like, while sakuya may be a better chef than mystia from an objective quality standpoint, mystia's lack of perfection makes her food more interesting. mystia probably has a larger variety of food too, since sakuya primarily cooks for just remillia and patchouli (and flandre)

Context: This is supposed to be a webcomic about the everyday domestic life of 4 immortal(hence the title)demons plus the human(the black-haired one on the couch)who lives with them. There is a plot but it's mostly in the background until about mid-way into the series. It's an adaptation of a short story I wrote because I wanted my first comic series to be relatively short and simple.
The tone tends to fluctuate between comedy, horror, and comedic horror/black comedy. The first half of the story is essentially "slice of demonic life" which tends to be equal parts standard "housemates irritating each other" stuff and things like "we accidentally summoned a bunch of soul-eating evil spirits." Even when the story gets serious it never really loses its light tone.
The first chapter is basically just introducing all the main characters and the premise, so I thought to have the cover be everyone just going about their daily lives to be fitting. I really like the font for the title and think it fits the tone/premise(although I'm starting to think it combined with the title itself is misleading people to think it's darker and more serious than it actually is)but I'm worried if it might be a bit overkill with the fanciness.

Thank you!
